title: Lyricists and who named the tunes
summary: Brown did not know the lyric writers, who came through the office, and says players knew tunes by Ellington's piano intros; Mills' claim to writing lyrics is mentioned.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: -- unfortunately. And Mitchell Parish who gets a credit on 'Sophisticated Lady' was the lyric writer, is that --
I didn't know him. I didn't know any of -- very few of the lyric writers that I know because they
were out of the office.
Uh-huh.
They were contacted by the office.
Do you remember how long after it was compiled that "Sophisticated Lady" was recorded?

No, not exactly because there were so many, many version and recordings made of it. I think they even made it into a waltz one time. Of course, I think that's when the -- the great Billy Strayhorn had come into the picture.
Uh-huh. Do you remember how long after it was a tune in its own right that it acquired lyrics?
No, but it wasn't too long because all successful music has to acquire lyrics, and the lyrics a lot of times make the tune. And very seldom does the music -- it alone make the tune.
Uh-huh. You said earlier that the tunes frequently got named in the office probably by Irving Mills. Is that what happened to the "Sophisticated Lady" as far as you know?

No, I don't -- I don't remember. See, we usually -- what we usually found out how -- when -- what the tune was going to be when he -- when Ellington would make some introductory piano phrases, then we'd automatically know what tune it was. We never paid any attention to names.
You -- there weren't -- when you heard the intro on the piano then you would look for the number in the book or --
No, well, this time --
-- was there a book?
Oh, yes. It was definitely a great big book, but by this time most of us knew the tune by heart.
Perhaps Mills' contribution to all these tunes which his names appears on is maybe he titled them, do you suppose?
I have no idea. No.
I saw a videotape interview with Irving Mills recently, and in it he said he wrote all the lyrics.
Oh, yeah? Well, goody goody. Goody goody.
Although I notice there is usually a lyric writer in addition to Irving Mills' name on most --
Yeah.
-- of the major numbers.
Well, your guess is as good as mine on that condition.
